title: Canonical Ext to derived-sections cohomology presentation
statement: For a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] and an abelian sheaf $F$ on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], use the common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Define $\operatorname{Ext}^q(\underline{\mathbb Z},F)\to H^q(R\Gamma(X,F[0]))$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] by the represented-derived-morphism evaluation [def-weil-pbc-derived-ext-evaluation] at the image of $1$ under the unit of the constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor]. Its additivity and bijectivity give the canonical additive equivalence, with inverse determined by this evaluation map. The evaluation in degree zero is evaluation at the integer generator, including for the empty scheme.

source.place: Tags 03FD and 01FT; derived global sections as Ext from the constant integer sheaf.

proof.text: Unfold sheafHToDerived and derivedExtEvaluation. Ext.homAddEquiv, the total right-derived functor and homology functors preserve addition; composition and evaluation in AddCommGrpCat preserve addition. This proves sheafHToDerived_add.

For an exact left adjoint L with additive right adjoint R, apply the defining derivedη_fac_app equation to M[0]. Naturality of the right-derived unit and the single-complex comparisons identify the derived adjunction unit, followed by R of the L-single comparison, with single(adj.unit) followed by rightDerivedSingleUnit. Applying zeroth homology and lem-sbc-right-derived-single-zero-unit identifies its map from M with adj.unit followed by the inverse of the canonical H0(RR(LM[0])) to R(LM) comparison. These are the proved private lemmas derived_unit_single and derived_unit_single_homology.

Set L to the constant-abelian-sheaf functor, R to global sections and P to ULift Z. L is exact and P is projective. Compose Ext.homEquiv, precomposition with L.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor, the canonical derived adjunction Hom equivalence, DerivedCategory.singleFunctorZeroHomEquiv for P, evaluation of Hom(P,-) at 1, the canonical derived shift and cohomology shift isomorphisms, and the singleFunctorIsoCompQ comparison. The preceding unit calculation proves that this composite is exactly sheafHToDerived, so it is bijective. All constructions apply to the empty scheme and every natural degree, including zero. This categorical argument is proved in the private generic helper derived_ext_evaluation_bijective and then specialized to the constant-sheaf adjunction, keeping concrete sheaf constructions abstract during kernel checking.

Apply Equiv.ofBijective to the explicit evaluation map and equip it with the proved additivity. Its inverse is uniquely determined by bijectivity, giving sheafHDerivedEquiv without any choice of unspecified cohomological data.
